page.text:
The continuity assumption in the converse is sufficient, not merely
decorative. Cauchy--Riemann equalities at one point do not by themselves
imply complex differentiability there. What matters is control of the
full two-dimensional error term, not only agreement of directional
derivatives along the coordinate axes.
